title: Pico the Penguin
moral: Being brave means trying even when you feel scared.

scenes.summary: Pico, a young penguin, is afraid of water despite living among swimmers.
scenes.text:
Pico the Penguin Who Was Afraid of Water

Far away in a land of snow and ice, lived a little penguin named Pico.

Pico had soft black-and-white feathers, tiny flippers, and bright, curious eyes.

But Pico had a secret…

He was afraid of water.

scenes.summary: Pico avoids swimming while others enjoy it and feels left out and hungry.
scenes.text:
All the other penguins loved swimming.

They splashed, dived, and zoomed through the icy sea.

“Come on, Pico!” called his friend Lolo. “The water is fun!”

But Pico shook his head.

“No, thank you,” he said. “It’s too cold… and too deep!”

Instead, Pico stayed on the ice, watching from far away.

One day, all the penguins went fishing together.

They jumped into the water—splash! splash! splash!

Pico stayed behind.

“I wish I could join them,” he said softly.

He looked at his tummy.

It rumbled.

“I’m hungry… but I can’t catch fish without swimming.”

Pico felt sad and alone.

scenes.summary: Nanu encourages Pico to be brave and helps him take small steps toward the water.
scenes.text:
Just then, an old penguin named Nanu waddled over.

“Why so gloomy, Pico?” Nanu asked kindly.

“I’m scared of water,” Pico admitted. “I want to swim, but I can’t.”

Nanu smiled.

“Being brave doesn’t mean you’re not scared,” he said. “It means you try, even when you are.”

Pico thought about that.

“Will you help me?” he asked.

“Of course,” said Nanu.

Nanu led Pico to the edge of the ice.

“Let’s start small,” he said.

Pico dipped one flipper into the water.

Brrr!

“It’s cold!” Pico squeaked.

“That’s okay,” Nanu said. “Try again.”

This time, Pico dipped both feet.

Then… slowly… he slid in.

Splash!

Pico panicked for a second.

“I’m in the water!” he cried.

But then…

He floated.

He kicked his little feet.

And guess what?

He didn’t sink.

“I’m doing it!” Pico shouted.

Lolo and the others cheered.

“Go, Pico!”

scenes.summary: Pico overcomes his fear, becomes a confident swimmer, and enjoys his success.

Soon, Pico was swimming, diving, and even catching fish!

“I’m not scared anymore,” he laughed.

Nanu smiled.

“You were always brave,” he said. “You just had to try.”

Pico beamed with pride.

That night, Pico ate the biggest, yummiest fish of all.

Being brave doesn’t mean you’re not scared.

It means trying, even when you are.

The End

story:
Pico the Penguin Who Was Afraid of Water

Far away in a land of snow and ice, lived a little penguin named Pico.

Pico had soft black-and-white feathers, tiny flippers, and bright, curious eyes.

But Pico had a secret…

He was afraid of water.

All the other penguins loved swimming.

They splashed, dived, and zoomed through the icy sea.

“Come on, Pico!” called his friend Lolo. “The water is fun!”

But Pico shook his head.

“No, thank you,” he said. “It’s too cold… and too deep!”

Instead, Pico stayed on the ice, watching from far away.

One day, all the penguins went fishing together.

They jumped into the water—splash! splash! splash!

Pico stayed behind.

“I wish I could join them,” he said softly.

He looked at his tummy.

It rumbled.

“I’m hungry… but I can’t catch fish without swimming.”

Pico felt sad and alone.

Just then, an old penguin named Nanu waddled over.

“Why so gloomy, Pico?” Nanu asked kindly.

“I’m scared of water,” Pico admitted. “I want to swim, but I can’t.”

Nanu smiled.

“Being brave doesn’t mean you’re not scared,” he said. “It means you try, even when you are.”

Pico thought about that.

“Will you help me?” he asked.

“Of course,” said Nanu.

Nanu led Pico to the edge of the ice.

“Let’s start small,” he said.

Pico dipped one flipper into the water.

Brrr!

“It’s cold!” Pico squeaked.

“That’s okay,” Nanu said. “Try again.”

This time, Pico dipped both feet.

Then… slowly… he slid in.

Splash!

Pico panicked for a second.

“I’m in the water!” he cried.

But then…

He floated.

He kicked his little feet.

And guess what?

He didn’t sink.

“I’m doing it!” Pico shouted.

Lolo and the others cheered.

“Go, Pico!”

Soon, Pico was swimming, diving, and even catching fish!

“I’m not scared anymore,” he laughed.

Nanu smiled.

“You were always brave,” he said. “You just had to try.”

Pico beamed with pride.

That night, Pico ate the biggest, yummiest fish of all.

Being brave doesn’t mean you’re not scared.

It means trying, even when you are.

The End
